# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 10 (LOGOS Formal)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 10
**Agent:** LOGOS (Formal Equivalence)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. Since Moses said: "You shall not eat swine, nor eagle, nor hawk, nor raven, nor any fish that has no scales" — he received three doctrines in understanding.
2. Moreover he says to them in Deuteronomy: "And I will establish my statutes as a covenant with this people." Therefore the commandment of God is not about the abstaining from eating; rather Moses spoke in the Spirit.
3. He mentioned the swine for this reason: do not associate, he says, with people who resemble pigs — who, while in want, forget the Lord, but when filled they remember him; just as the pig, while it is eating, does not know its master, but when it is hungry it cries aloud, then when it receives food it is silent again.
4. "Neither the eagle, nor the hawk, nor the kite, nor the raven shall you eat." You shall not, he says, associate with or become like such persons who do not know how to acquire their food through labor and sweat, but who snatch the goods of others by violent means, yet seem to walk about in all innocence while watching for those they may strip with their greediness — just as these birds do not procure their food by labor but sit idle and seek to consume the flesh of others, being pests in their wickedness.
5. "And you shall not eat," he says, "the lamprey, the polypus, or the cuttlefish." You shall not, he says, become like those people — who are already wholly condemned and godless, who cling to this world as though it were desirable; just as these fish alone are accursed, lurking in the deep water, not swimming as other fish do but dwelling in the mud at the bottom.
6. "You shall not eat the hare." Why? Do not become a corrupter of children, nor like such persons; for the hare gains an additional orifice each year, and has therefore as many of them as it has years of age.
7. "Nor shall you eat the hyena." Do not become, he says, an adulterer or a seducer, nor become like such persons. Why? Because this creature changes its nature year by year, and becomes male at one time and female at another.
8. And the weasel also he rightly hated. Do not become like those who, as we hear, commit lawlessness with the mouth; do not associate with unclean women who practice iniquity with the mouth — for this animal conceives through the mouth.
9. Moses received these as spiritual commandments; but they, following the desire of the flesh, received them as commandments about eating.
10. But David also received knowledge of the three doctrines and says in the same manner: "Blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the ungodly and does not stand in the way of sinners" — just as the fish that lurk in the deep in darkness — "and does not sit in the seat of the scornful" — just as those birds that sit and wait for prey.
11. You now have the full teaching about food.
